title: Critical: PipeWire frame buffer leak and data race in on_process()
description: capture_pipewire.c:604-610 on_process() overwrites pending_frame/held_pw_buf if a previous frame is still unreleased. The old PipeWire buffer is never requeued, causing buffer starvation/leak and data lifetime races. Also pw_stop() does not signal frame_cond before join (line 814-826), blocking get_frame(). Init failure paths (710-726) leak partially-created core/stream/portal resources.

title: nostrc: event-driven AUTH-OK recovery for protected pool subscriptions
description: Metadesk md-xcy dependency. Current libnostr/src/relay.c nostr_relay_auth calls nostr_relay_publish (EVENT, not AUTH), takes a signing callback without userdata, and has no AUTH-specific acknowledgement helper. AUTH envelope serialization + relay_write + per-relay OK callback let Metadesk sign off-reader and observe acceptance/rejection without editing nostrc. However simplepool.c pool_drain_all retires/frees CLOSED subscriptions, while pool_reconcile_subs blindly refires missing subscriptions on a <=200ms cadence, even before AUTH succeeds or after AUTH/restricted rejection. get_callback_subscription is borrowed only within middleware/state callback, not an owned event-driven retry handle. Need an AUTH-result-aware per-relay subscription pause/resume/retry API (or pool-owned AUTH bridge with userdata/cancellation) that reissues protected REQ exactly on successful current-generation AUTH OK, not timer polling, and leaves rejection closed until a new challenge/explicit action. Include private relay rejection/re-auth/CLOSED and reconnect tests. Do not modify nostrc sources in Metadesk work.
notes: 2026-11-18: user decided to lift Groundhog's GhRelayScope/GhRelayAuthSigner approach into libnostr under nostrc bead nostrc-7i6w (scope recorded there as design). md-1be is satisfied when nostrc-7i6w lands; metadesk then adopts the library API to close md-xcy.

title: client: overlay+video use two separate SDL_RenderPresent calls -> ghost trails + mis-scaled video
description: on_decoded() calls md_renderer_present() (clear+copy video+present) while the main loop's render_client_overlay()->render_draw_data() does a second SDL_RenderPresent() after drawing ImGui, with no clear or video redraw. title: host: capture thread exits before PipeWire stream reaches STREAMING (frames=0, black screen)
description: capture_thread_func()'s loop guard is md_capture_is_active(), which is only true once on_state_changed sees PW_STREAM_STATE_STREAMING. host_wait_capture_dimensions() returns as soon as on_param_changed sets width/height (during format negotiation, before STREAMING), so the thread is spawned while active is still false and exits immediately — the stream delivers frames into pending_frame but nobody consumes them (host frames=0 sent=0, client black screen). Reproduced cross-host: Mac client ↔ Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME Wayland VM; link active, format BGRx 1512x909 negotiated, yet 0 frames. Native fast Linux usually wins the race. Fix: capture thread waits up to ~5s for active before its pull loop.
close_reason: Fixed in d358f1a; verified by live cross-host stream (Ubuntu VM host -> macOS client)

title: host: odd capture dimensions (e.g. 1512x909) make encoder creation fail

title: macOS: libnsync's clock_gettime shadows libSystem, so CLOCK_MONOTONIC reads wall time project-wide
description: Why: Homebrew libnsync 1.30 exports _clock_gettime, and on macOS it ignores the clock id and returns gettimeofday wall time. ld binds each undefined symbol to the first dylib in link order that exports it, and nsync (dep_nsync, meson.build:183) comes before libSystem. So libmetadesk and every tool or test linking it resolve clock_gettime to libnsync. Check with: nm -m build/libmetadesk.0.dylib | grep clock_gettime, which shows '(from libnsync)'. Found during md-6c4f: tools/capture_frame's CLOCK_MONOTONIC read returned 1.795e18 ns (epoch). Impact: every clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) on macOS is wall time, so NTP slews and steps and manual clock changes move deadlines and timeouts. Affected: io_util.h, stream.c (2 sites), fips_control.c (2), host/main.c (3), client/main.c, mcp_resources.c, the tests test_mcp/test_host_binding/test_atspi/mcp_proxy_host_fixture, and tools atspi_dump/encode_roundtrip. Linux is unaffected: Linux libnsync only imports clock_gettime@GLIBC. What: either (a) give one shared md_monotonic_ns() (io_util.h) that uses clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) on __APPLE__ and route every site through it (md_capture_clock_ns in capture.c already does this for frame timestamps), or (b) fix link resolution on darwin so libSystem wins, e.g. link -lSystem ahead of nsync, then verify with nm -m. Add a regression check that the monotonic clock is not wall time (test_capture's test_frame_clock has the pattern).
close_reason: Fixed in d730d08 on fix/md-5aua-monotonic-clock (unmerged). (a) md_time.{h,c}: md_monotonic_ns()/md_now_ms()/md_cond_*. Every caller converted; md_capture_clock_ns aliases it. (b) darwin links -lSystem before libnsync, and nm -m shows from libSystem. tests/test_time.c plus the darwin nm test fail when either fix is reverted. macOS 36/36, Linux 36/36 parallel and serial. Follow-up: md-l4f4 (nostr.c wait_history).

title: SendInput targets the primary monitor only; wrong with --capture-output on a non-primary output
description: Why: md-346 added MdCaptureConfig.output / --capture-output so DXGI can capture any attached output, but input_sendinput.cpp maps client coordinates with MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE normalised to screen_w/h and no MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK, which addresses the primary monitor. Capturing a non-primary output therefore sends clicks to the wrong place. What: expose the captured output's virtual-desktop rect from the capture HAL (e.g. an origin in MdCaptureCtx or a getter; DxgiState.output_desc.DesktopCoordinates has it), pass it into MdInputConfig, and normalise against the virtual desktop (SM_X/Y/CX/CYVIRTUALSCREEN) with MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK. Test with the SendInput recorder (never inject real input).
close_reason: Committed on feat/windows-w65-dbg-246: DXGI publishes the physical output rect via md-xat's md_capture_get_output_rect; SendInput maps with md_input_map_to_output and normalises across the physical virtual desktop with MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK (pixel-centre, exact round-trip). Recorder + synthetic GetSystemMetrics tests; clang/MSVC/session 0/console/macOS green apart from pre-existing flake md-4dsa.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Coordination from md-xat (branch feat/md-xat-sck-output, macOS). It adds HAL plumbing that DXGI can reuse instead of inventing parallel names. (1) capture.h: typedef MdCaptureRect {int32_t x,y; uint32_t width,height}, MdCaptureCtx.output_rect (backend sets it in start), and md_capture_get_output_rect(ctx,&rect). DXGI can fill it from output_desc.DesktopCoordinates. (2) input.h: MdInputConfig gains int32_t output_x, output_y and uint32_t output_width, output_height, plus a pure md_input_map_to_output(cfg,x,y,&gx,&gy) (clamp + offset/scale into global desktop space). (3) host/main.c: copies the rect into input_cfg next to screen_width/height. (4) input.c: md_input_execute_action now treats click coordinates as GLOBAL (accessibility) coordinates. With output bounds set, it inverse-maps them to frame space and refuses points off the captured output, because the stream-mode agent shares the host MdInput. SendInput can map gx/gy to VIRTUALDESK normalised coordinates. Expect overlap in capture.h, input.h/input.c and that host/main.c hunk.

title: Client accepts a stale session_accept replayed from relay history
description: Found by md-ah9.11. The client's gift-wrap subscription uses since=now-2d (NIP-59 window) and takes the first session_accept DM from the host; it does not correlate the accept with its current request. Against a relay that retains history, a second negotiation for the same host/client pair (new host process) replays the previous session's accept: client logged 'session accepted (id=0929f5ec...)' while the live host had reserved 6531447f...; client sent the stale proof, host 'rejected unproven client #1', client 'ERROR: failed to send session info'. Fails closed (no auth bypass), but repeat sessions within two days fail on retaining relays. Related deferred P3.8 request-ID/correlation work (docs/stream-binding.md); no bead tracked it. md-ah9.11 used a fresh private relay per cell to avoid it.
acceptance_criteria: Client only accepts a session_accept bound to its own current request (request id/nonce or rumor freshness); a test replays an old accept over a retaining relay and the next negotiation still succeeds
close_reason: Fixed on fix/md-6ns-stale-accept (1706481, rebased on master c6d6ba1): request_id/issued_at/expires_at correlation (v1, session-v2 field shapes); client accepts only its current request's answer; host answers only live (post-EOSE) fresh requests without latching on history; dedup live-upgrade for history-first copies. Retaining-relay + two-relay tests and second real host/client e2e on same relay pass on macOS/Linux/ASan. Follow-ups: md-cdz (container same-relay cell), md-tiy (fips_addr UBSan).

title: NIP-5F signer cannot decrypt NIP-17 session requests: nostrc client returns JSON-escaped strings
description: Found by md-ah9.11. nostrc nips/nip5f/src/core/sock_client.c nostr_nip5f_client_nip44_decrypt (and nip44_encrypt) strip the surrounding quotes of the JSON string result but never unescape it. Any plaintext containing a double quote comes back as {\"... so a NIP-5F-backed host rejects every NIP-17 gift wrap: '[json] event parse failed: compact: expected , or closing delimiter (offset 2)' then 'nostr: DM rejected: invalid-seal'. A server cannot avoid this (JSON strings must escape quotes). Same code at the VM nostrc build da2e4d62 and local nostrc 120ca9672. docs/accounts.md lists nip5f as a host/client backend, so NIP-5F hosts/clients cannot negotiate sessions; access CLI signing works (no decrypt). The md-pss access_cli private relay test never decrypts, so it does not catch this.
acceptance_criteria: nostrc NIP-5F client JSON-unescapes string results (or parses result with a JSON parser); a metadesk test negotiates a host session through a NIP-5F signer whose decrypted seal contains quotes

title: MCP: gate action tools on the principal's input grant (per-request caps)
description: md-ah9.3 admits NIP-98 MCP principals whose host-allowlist grant includes agent, but MCP has no per-principal tool gating: an admitted principal gets the whole tool surface (actions unless --no-input/no input backend). For video sessions, agent without input hides actions (docs/access.md). The MCP HTTP authorizer should return the principal's capability mask (static/bearer = host policy), and tools/call of non-read tools (mcp_tools.c read_kind==0) must require MD_CAP_INPUT, with tools/list filtered per principal. Needs a caller-context variant of md_mcp_server_handle_message_with_sink. See docs/mcp-auth.md 'Scope note'.

Rules: live host-allowlist NIP-98 principals get their current v1 grant, read afresh on every request; admission needs agent; read tools/resources need agent; the 9 action tools need agent+input. Static npub/file, bearer, credential-less loopback and stdio get all caps, still subject to --no-input/input readiness (operator credentials with no grant vocabulary; keeps existing deployments). Agent-only: tools/list omits actions; tools/call returns isError 'requires the 'input' grant' with no handler run. Grant changes apply to the next request; SSE recheck needs agent; session-info is caller-narrowed. Gates: macOS meson test 35/35 (all signer backends); Linux VM 36 OK + 1 opt-in skip (access session e2e), parallel (-j2/2 procs) and serial; ASan+UBSan (LSan on Linux) MCP tests 5/5 on both. nostr-protocol-smells diff review: clean. Follow-up: md-ht7 (tools/list_changed).

title: Upstream report: libatspi 2.52 get_application pending call is not released by atspi_exit
description: Follow-up to md-x16: report to GNOME at-spi2-core upstream. AT_SPI2_CORE_2_52_0 atspi/atspi-misc.c get_application (427/434) calls dbus_connection_send_with_reply(GetApplicationBusAddress), retains the caller-owned DBusPendingCall reference and installs handle_get_bus_address with no destroy notifier. Only that callback unrefs it. handle_get_bus_address likewise creates GetItems pending calls whose reference is only released by handle_get_items. Neither cleanup()/atspi_exit nor atspi_application_dispose tracks/cancels/unrefs these requests. If connection teardown prevents callback dispatch, the retained pending call keeps its connection/error reply/timeout allocations alive. Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 libatspi build-id d0fdcf72be49abfb6f06898b37e3708b3eb00df3 debug info maps offsets 0x17258/0x1727c to get_application (not GetItems); caller _atspi_ref_accessible at 0x1bd10. Baseline 15/1000 mode2 failures, 871 bytes/6 indirect allocations, predates md-dzm. Source https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/at-spi2-core/-/blob/AT_SPI2_CORE_2_52_0/atspi/atspi-misc.c . Attach independent libatspi-only reproducer and diagnostic results from md-x16 before upstream submission. Public API provides no handle or pending-call drain/cancel operation; do not change metadesk dispatcher lifetime or add timer-based workaround. Verify upstream fix then remove private-test-only exact-frame LSan suppression.
close_reason: Invalid: not an upstream bug. The stranded get_application pending call is caused by metadesk calling libatspi off its dispatch thread (md-x16, fixed in b0f7f26 by walking on the default context). Single-threaded libatspi use cannot complete the call between send_with_reply and set_notify. No suppression or upstream report needed.

title: Linux VM MCP HTTP test has fragile port/deadline gates
description: Observed during md-pss qualification on 192.168.64.3 (Ubuntu arm64), all signer backends enabled. Default parallel full suite: MCP HTTP+SSE transport timed out at 15.15s (34 other tests passed). Serial full suite: test_mcp_http.c:1178 http != NULL failed, then auth_status/connect/read-budget assertions at 1182-1197 (15/625 failed); 34 other tests passed. Untouched 5966e40 baseline built separately under ~/wt-pss/baseline passed the targeted test in 14.57s, close to its existing 15s Meson timeout. No MCP or AT-SPI source/test edits in md-pss. Investigate fixed/dynamic port reservation and test timing; do not simply relax production authorization deadlines. Gate logs /tmp/md-pss-linux-tests.log, /tmp/md-pss-linux-serial.log, /tmp/md-pss-baseline-test.log on VM.
close_reason: Fixed in 18fe3af. Root cause: (1) slowness ~14 s vs a 15 s timeout: each case's shutdown waited out the accept loop's 1 s select poll (13 x ~1.0 s); (2) failures: the fixed port range 18710+ meant any foreign listener or concurrent checkout caused create to fail, and the NULL server then cascaded (15/631). title: MCP bridge destroy does not unsubscribe a11y change callback (use-after-free on teardown)
description:
Why: md_mcp_bridge_create() registers md_mcp_a11y_change_cb with the bridge (or its resource ctx) as userdata via md_a11y_subscribe_changes(config->a11y, ...) (src/core/mcp_bridge.c:98). md_mcp_bridge_destroy() (mcp_bridge.c:173-) tears down transports, tool contexts, server, and agent but never detaches that subscription, and src/core/a11y.h exposes no unsubscribe API at all (only int (*subscribe_changes) in the vtable and md_a11y_subscribe_changes). Because the host keeps the MdA11yCtx alive and destroys it only after the bridge (src/host/main.c ~:790), any backend change event delivered in that window — AT-SPI event, AXObserver notification, UIA COM event — invokes the callback with a freed bridge/resource pointer. Surfaced by the md-52m engineer while adding snapshot invalidation to the callback (which widens the window since the callback now touches the snapshot too).

What: (1) add md_a11y_unsubscribe_changes(MdA11yCtx*, MdA11yChangeCb, void*) (or make subscribe return a handle) to a11y.h and implement it in all three backends — a11y_atspi.c (atspi_event_listener_deregister), a11y_axui.m (AXObserverRemoveNotification / CFRunLoopRemoveSource), a11y_uia.cpp (RemoveAutomationEventHandler / RemoveFocusChangedEventHandler); the backends must guarantee no callback runs after unsubscribe returns (join or synchronize with the dispatch thread). (2) Call it first thing in md_mcp_bridge_destroy(), before freeing anything the callback can touch. (3) Test in tests/test_mcp.c with the fake backend: after bridge destroy, firing a fake change event must not invoke the callback (use a counting hook).
acceptance_criteria: a11y.h has an unsubscribe API implemented by all three backends; md_mcp_bridge_destroy unsubscribes before teardown; test asserts no callback after destroy; all tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to master as 39f2458 (93d07b9, 05b5c0d, 9a0240e). md_a11y_unsubscribe_changes with in-flight drain; bridge detaches first. UIA backend change uncompiled on macOS — verify on a Windows build. 22/22 unit + live AX test pass

title: Spike: run metadesk host/client inside containers (headless capture, input, FIPS, OCI runtime)
description:
Why: metadesk should run inside containers — both a containerized HOST (expose a container's desktop/app to agents + humans) and a containerized CLIENT (esp. agent/MCP). This is a runtime/architecture problem distinct from the packaging-format spike (md-kb7); md-kb7 only owns 'publish OCI images' as a distribution channel, this spike owns 'make it actually work headless in a container'. Strongly aligned with the AI-agent use case: a sandboxed container workload an agent drives headlessly via MCP + a11y.

What (spike — prototype + recommend):
- HOST in container:
  - Capture without a physical display: headless Wayland compositor (wlroots/cage/gnome headless), Xvfb+X11 capture, or a nested compositor; vs host-socket passthrough.
  - PipeWire + xdg-desktop-portal inside the container (own instance vs bind-mounting host sockets), ScreenCast consent in a non-interactive/headless context (restore_token, or portal backend that auto-grants).
  - Input injection without bare-metal /dev/uinput + CAP: wlroots virtual-pointer/virtual-keyboard protocols, ydotool, or inject into the nested compositor; device passthrough tradeoffs.
  - AT-SPI accessibility bus inside the container.
  - FIPS: TUN in the container netns (CAP_NET_ADMIN, /dev/net/tun) vs a FIPS sidecar sharing the network namespace; or direct IP only.
- CLIENT in container:
  - Agent/MCP client (no display) — primary, mostly networking.
  - Human client with display — GPU/display passthrough (DRI, Wayland/X socket) or stream-to-browser; likely out of initial scope.
- Runtime targets: Docker, Podman (incl. rootless), Kubernetes (Pod spec, securityContext, device plugins, service exposure), systemd-nspawn.
- Security: minimize capabilities, rootless where possible, document the privilege each feature requires.
- Reference deployments: Dockerfile(s)/compose + a k8s manifest for the headless-agent host scenario.

Deliverable: a design doc (docs/designs/) with a recommended headless-capture + input + FIPS architecture per runtime, a capability/privilege matrix, the consent/permission story for non-interactive hosts, example Dockerfile/compose/k8s manifests, and a phased plan with spin-off issues. Coordinate with md-kb7 (OCI images as a channel) and md-5zi (add container cells to the E2E matrix).

title: Spike: cross-platform distribution packaging — no-build-from-source install on all major platforms (incl. Omarchy)
description:
Why: today metadesk is source-only (meson + ninja, with a hand-built nostrc tree and system FFmpeg/SDL2/libyuv/etc.). Adoption requires simple, no-compile installs — users should get a signed, pre-built package per platform, not a build environment. ('non-FYC' = not 'fetch-your-compiler'/from-source.)

What (spike — survey, prototype, and recommend; not full build-out):
- Define per-platform packaging + delivery channels:
  - macOS: signed + notarized .app in a .dmg; Homebrew cask. (metadesk-host + metadesk-client.)
  - Windows: signed installer (MSI/EXE or MSIX) + winget manifest.
  - Linux (distro-agnostic): Flatpak on Flathub (portal/PipeWire/ScreenCast fit GNOME well) and/or AppImage for portable use.
  - Debian/Ubuntu: .deb + apt repo/PPA.
  - Fedora/RHEL: .rpm + Copr/dnf repo.
  - Arch + Omarchy: AUR package (pacman); validate on Omarchy's Hyprland/Wayland stack (xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland for ScreenCast, wlroots input).
- Dependency strategy: bundle vs system for FFmpeg, SDL2, libyuv, secp256k1, libwebsockets, cJSON, libb2, nostrc (currently an uninstalled build-tree dep — needs a proper installable/vendored story), and the GUI toolkit if the UX spike (md-70v) adds one.
- External runtime deps that are NOT bundled: the FIPS daemon (document how users get it per platform) and screen-capture permissions/portals per OS.
- Code signing / notarization / reproducibility; versioning; auto-update strategy (Sparkle/winget/Flatpak/repo updates).
- CI/CD: a release pipeline that builds + signs + publishes artifacts for every target from tags.

Deliverable: a design doc (docs/designs/) with a recommended channel per platform, the dependency-bundling decision matrix, signing/notarization plan, auto-update approach, a CI release-pipeline sketch, and a phased rollout with spin-off issues. Include an explicit Omarchy/Hyprland validation checklist. Coordinate with md-70v (UX/toolkit choice affects packaging) and md-5zi (per-platform E2E).

title: Spike: host/client management UX — identity/keys, connecting to hosts, address book, parity with remote-desktop tools
description:
Why: the current client/host are CLI-only (npub/IP args, op:// secrets, manual signer flags). To be usable like mainstream remote-desktop packages (RustDesk, Parsec, AnyDesk, RealVNC, Moonlight), metadesk needs real management UX for identity and connections on BOTH ends.

What (spike — explore + propose, not full build):
- Identity & key handling: generate/import/rotate Nostr keypairs (nsec/npub), secure at-rest storage (keychain/1Password/secret-service), unlock flow, display npub/fingerprint, signer selection (NIP-46 bunker, NIP-55L, NIP-5F, local).
- Connect-to-host flow: enter/scan an npub or IP, trust-on-first-use prompt, saved credentials, connection status/errors surfaced clearly (FIPS readiness, auth, route).
- Host address book: named saved hosts (npub/IP, last-connected, tags, per-host capabilities/notes), favorites, quick-connect, import/export.
- Host side: approve/deny incoming clients, NIP-51 allowlist management UI, session list/kick, per-client granted capabilities.
- General parity: settings (resolution/bitrate/fps), reconnect UX, clipboard, multi-monitor selection, in-overlay connection manager.

Deliverable: a design doc (docs/designs/) covering IA, flows, where it lives (ImGui overlay vs separate GTK/native app vs both), data model for the address book, security model for key storage, and a phased implementation plan with issues to spin off. Survey 2-3 comparable tools for UX patterns.
design:
Nostr-native constraint: prefer Nostr protocol primitives over bespoke mechanisms wherever practical.

- NIP-05: human-readable host identifiers (user@domain) that resolve to the host npub, so users connect to 'host@example.com' instead of a raw npub. Support NIP-05 verification/display in the connect flow and address book.
- NIP-51 (lists): use standard list events for the host allowlist/approved clients and for the client-side host address book / favorites / tags (e.g. categorized people/relay/app-specific sets) rather than a local-only format. Lists sync across a user's devices via relays.
- NIP-78 (application-specific data, kind 30078): store metadesk app/config data and address-book/host metadata as replaceable app-data events, so settings and saved hosts follow the identity across devices.
- NIP-44: encrypt any private payloads (address book contents, per-host notes/credentials, app-data, non-public list entries) with NIP-44 before publishing to relays. Nothing sensitive leaves the device in cleartext.
- Keep the existing session-negotiation stack (NIP-44-encrypted DMs, NIP-17 where applicable) and signer abstractions (NIP-46/55L/5F) as the identity/signing backbone.

Design doc must map each UX feature to the Nostr primitive it uses (and justify any case where a non-Nostr/local mechanism is chosen instead), plus relay strategy (which relays, user-configurable, NIP-65 outbox considerations) and offline/first-run behavior when no relay is reachable.
notes: 2026-11-16 decision (user): metadesk supports a signer interface like Groundhog/GNostr and lets the user decide which key is used for what. title: Testing: end-to-end host↔client matrix across Windows/GNOME/macOS/Omarchy over IP and FIPS
description:
Why: metadesk host/client has been exercised mostly on a single pairing (macOS client ↔ Ubuntu/GNOME VM host over direct IP). We need a documented, repeatable end-to-end test matrix that covers every supported platform as both host and client, over both transports, so regressions in capture, encode/decode, a11y, input injection, session negotiation, and FIPS routing are caught.

What: Define and run an E2E matrix.
- Roles × platforms: each of {Windows, GNOME/Linux, macOS, Omarchy (Hyprland/Wayland Linux)} as HOST and as CLIENT.
- Transports: (a) direct IP (LAN/IPv6 over TUN-less path), (b) FIPS mesh (npub, NIP-44 session negotiation, TCP over FIPS TUN).
- Per-cell checks: connect/auth, video (frames flow, correct dims, fills window, no trails), decode/FPS/bitrate, overlay, HUMAN input (mouse move/button/scroll + keyboard, correct button mapping, 1:1 cursor mapping), AGENT path (MCP tools, a11y tree, action-by-id), reconnect/restore, clean teardown.
- Capture consent/permissions per platform (ScreenCaptureKit TCC, PipeWire portal/restore_token, DXGI, Omarchy/Hyprland portal).

Acceptance: a results matrix (pass/fail + notes per cell), repeatable run steps/scripts, and a filed bug per failing cell. Note known-flaky areas (GNOME screencast restore, see md-3nv) explicitly.

title: client/host mouse: left-click sent as right-click; cursor X diverges when window != frame size
description:
Two mouse bugs found testing macOS client <-> Ubuntu VM:

1. Left click registered as right-click: uinput_mouse_button() uses 0=left,1=right,2=middle, but the client wire sends 1=left and the host handler called md_input_click(...,1) => BTN_RIGHT. Fixed: host maps wire buttons {1=left,2=mid,3=right} to md_input {0=left,2=mid,1=right}.

2. Remote cursor X diverges from the client cursor, growing with distance from the origin: map_to_remote() used the renderer's stored window size (set to the frame size by ensure_texture), but when the OS keeps the window at a different size than the frame (e.g. not shrunk to 1280 while the video is stretched to fill a 1512-wide window), mouse coords (0..1512) were divided by the stale 1280 -> remote moved ~1.18x too fast. Fixed: map_to_remote() now uses the live SDL_GetWindowSize, matching the space the video is stretched into and the space SDL reports mouse events in. Verified via libinput that the host uinput absolute mapping is itself linear/correct.
close_reason: Fixed: host button-convention mapping (left no longer right-click); client map_to_remote uses live SDL_GetWindowSize so cursor tracks when window!=frame. Host uinput mapping verified linear via libinput.

title: host: streaming unreliable across client reconnects and restored screencast sessions
description:
Two failure modes seen bringing up the macOS client against an Ubuntu VM host:

1. MULTI-CLIENT STALL: on each client disconnect the host calls md_encoder_flush(), which sends avcodec_send_frame(NULL) (EOF) to the PERSISTENT encoder. The next client's md_encoder_submit then fails silently (encoder in draining/EOF state) -> frames=0 sent=0, black client. Fresh single-client start works; the 2nd+ client gets nothing.

2. RESTORED-SCREENCAST IDLE: a PipeWire screencast restored via restore_token sometimes comes up with its node idle / unlinked, so capture delivers no frames even though md_capture_start succeeded (host frames=0 with a client connected). A fresh interactive consent streams reliably.

Hardening: (a) don't flush the persistent encoder to EOF per client; force a keyframe for each new client instead so they get an immediate IDR; (b) make pw_stop tear down per-start resources so md_capture_stop+start is a clean restart; (c) add a host capture watchdog that restarts capture when no frames arrive for several seconds while a client is connected, and after repeated failures clears the saved restore_token so the next start re-prompts for consent.
notes: Implemented: (a) encoder no longer flushed to EOF per client; force-keyframe on new connect (encode.c/h, host); (b) pw_stop tears down stream/core/portal so md_capture_stop+start restarts cleanly; (c) host capture watchdog restarts capture on stall and clears restore_token after repeated failures (capture.h/c vtable + pw_forget_authorization). Watchdog + token-clear verified live on the VM (restart x2 then cleared token with operator guidance). Multi-client frame-flow not live-verified this session — the GNOME screencast restore_token proved flaky and fresh consent requires an interactive click that wasn't available; encoder-EOF root cause is proven and unit tests pass 21/21.

title: client overlay: dragging broken (vertical-only + jump) from mismatched video/overlay render scale
description: After the single-present change, md_renderer_begin_frame drew the video at SDL scale 1.0 with a pixel viewport while render_draw_data drew the overlay at scale 2.0 (DisplayFramebufferScale). ImGui lays out and hit-tests in logical points; drawing the overlay in a different effective space than ImGui expected made the panel's grab math wrong — the title bar could only be dragged vertically and jumped ~50px on mousedown. Fix: render the whole frame (video + overlay) in one space — begin_frame sets a full-output viewport then the HiDPI scale, draws the video to a point-sized dst, and render_draw_data no longer touches the scale.
close_reason: Fixed in unified-coordinate render; verified live: overlay drags correctly in both axes with no jump, video still fills window

title: host: PipeWire screencast needs interactive consent every run (no restore_token)
description: portal_screencast_open() requested persist_mode=0, so every host start shows the GNOME 'Share your screen' dialog; unattended, the Start call times out after 60s and capture falls back to a no-op direct connect (frames=0, black client). Fix: request persist_mode=2 and persist the returned restore_token under XDG_STATE_HOME, reusing it on later runs so consent is remembered after one approval.

title: client: human mouse/keyboard input is never forwarded to the host
description: The human video client displays the remote desktop but captures no input: there is no MD_PKT_INPUT packet, and client/main.c never translates SDL mouse/keyboard events into anything sent to the host. The host already has md_input wired (uinput/CGEvent/SendInput) via the agent, so only a raw-input packet + client capture + host injection are missing. Implement MD_PKT_INPUT carrying mouse move/button/wheel and key/text; forward on the client (skipping events ImGui consumes) mapped to remote coords; inject on the host via md_input_*.
close_reason: Fixed and verified live: video fills window, single-present (no trails), restore_token skips consent, mouse/keyboard forwarded (remote cursor tracks + hover responds, host rx grows)

title: MCP: add targeted a11y query tools and stop pinning tree format to JSON
description:
Why: an MCP agent today has exactly one way to read the UI tree — the whole metadesk://ui-tree resource (src/core/mcp_resources.c:26-56) — and the nine metadesk_* action tools (src/core/mcp_tools.c:315-333) return either a JSON delta or the whole tree. There is no node-level or filtered read path, so the model must scan every node to find a target, paying full token cost per read. The host also hard-pins MCP to MD_TREE_FORMAT_JSON (src/host/main.c:762), so the token-efficient compact format (md_a11y_to_compact, src/core/a11y.c:554) is never available to agents even though the bridge/resources already support it (mcp_resources.c:37-45). Considered and rejected: GraphQL over MCP — LLMs mis-author query strings, GraphQL has no recursive fragments for tree traversal, no lightweight C parser exists, and it would bypass MCP per-tool JSON Schema validation. Targeted tools over the existing MdA11yNode tree get ~90% of the value with zero new dependencies. Origin: docs/investigations/a11y-xml-ingestion-claim-2026-11-13.md follow-up discussion.

What:
1. New read tools in src/core/mcp_tools.c, all operating on md_a11y_walk() output (or a cached snapshot) with the existing serializers:
   - metadesk_find(role?, label_contains?, state?, limit=50, format=compact|json) — server-side filter; returns matching nodes (flat list, compact lines by default).
   - metadesk_subtree(id, depth=2, format) — scoped traversal rooted at a node id.
   - metadesk_node(id) — full JSON detail for one node (role, label, states, bounds, child count).
   - metadesk_focused() — the node carrying the 'focused' state plus its ancestor window.
   - metadesk_windows() — top-level windows/frames (role, label, id, bounds).
   Each tool gets a JSON Schema in its registration so arguments are validated by the MCP layer; shared helpers (find_node_by_id already exists in agent.c:47-57) should move to a11y.c or a small a11y_query.c rather than be duplicated.
2. Format pinning: remove the hard-coded MD_TREE_FORMAT_JSON at src/host/main.c:762. Make the MCP bridge default to compact for the ui-tree resource and tool text results, with a per-call 'format' argument on the read tools and a host CLI/config switch for the resource default. Keep application/json vs text/plain mimeType selection in mcp_resources.c:143-144 consistent with the chosen format.
3. Tests in tests/test_mcp.c: find by role/label/state with limit, subtree depth bounds, node-not-found error shape, focused/windows on a fixture tree, and resource mimeType matching the configured format.
4. Docs: add the new tools and the format switch to docs/AGENT_API.md and the MCP section of docs/metadesk-spec.md.

Depends on / interacts with: md-qqz (compact sessions get JSON deltas) — the compact default for MCP tool results must not reintroduce that mismatch; tool results that are deltas should stay JSON or be clearly discriminated. md-1kg (subscribe_changes unimplemented) — once live, agents should prefer pushed deltas + targeted reads over full re-reads.
acceptance_criteria: Five new read tools registered with JSON Schemas and covered by test_mcp; MD_TREE_FORMAT_JSON no longer hard-coded in src/host/main.c; MCP ui-tree resource and read tools default to compact with a working per-call/host override; mimeType matches format; AGENT_API.md documents the tools; all tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to master as fdb4946; 5 read tools, a11y_query.{c,h}, --mcp-tree-format, review fixes in cd6c2c8; 22/22 tests

title: Compact-format sessions receive JSON deltas the client cannot patch
description:
Why: agent_render_update_locked() (src/core/agent.c:220-244) and md_agent_send_delta() (agent.c:338-362) always emit JSON via md_a11y_delta_to_json() regardless of agent->tree_format. A client that negotiated MD_TREE_FORMAT_COMPACT (src/client/main.c:205,220) caches a compact plain-text snapshot in ctx.ui_tree_json (client/main.c:732-740) and then calls md_a11y_tree_patch() (client/main.c:760) which begins with cJSON_Parse(tree_json) (src/core/a11y.c:699) — the compact snapshot fails to parse, patch returns NULL, and the client silently keeps the stale tree. Spec docs/metadesk-spec.md §3.3.3 says deltas use 'the same formats above', which the implementation does not do.

Currently dormant: the stock video client never sends MD_PKT_ACTION, and the MCP host pins MD_TREE_FORMAT_JSON (src/host/main.c:762). It becomes active for any stream consumer that negotiates compact and submits actions.

What: (a) in agent.c, make the update policy format-aware — for compact sessions send a full compact snapshot (MD_PKT_UI_TREE) instead of a JSON delta, in both agent_render_update_locked() and md_agent_send_delta(); (b) correct spec §3.3.3 to document JSON deltas for JSON sessions and full-snapshot replacement for compact sessions (or design a real compact delta contract + consumer); (c) add a test in tests/test_agent.c covering a compact-negotiated agent after an action. Found during docs/investigations/a11y-xml-ingestion-claim-2026-11-13.md.
acceptance_criteria: Compact-negotiated agent never emits MD_PKT_UI_TREE_DELTA with JSON payload; spec §3.3.3 matches implementation; test_agent covers compact post-action update.
close_reason: Merged to master as 8129758 (commits 9864e03,12be22b for md-qqz; a365ef0,b1b665f for md-52m); 22/22 tests

title: nostrc/libfiber: add fiber-parking recvfrom/sendto/recvmsg/sendmsg
description:
Target repo: nostrc (libgo/fiber). Filed here because metadesk is the consumer and the investigation lives in nostrc docs/investigations/fips-rust-to-c-port-on-nostrc-2026-11-13.md (branch feature/fips).

Why: libfiber's netpoller-aware I/O surface is only gof_read, gof_write, gof_connect and gof_accept (libgo/fiber/include/libgo/fiber.h). There is no datagram API: a fiber doing UDP must either block the worker thread on recvfrom/sendmsg or hand-roll the park/wake cycle. Any FIPS-style UDP transport (per-peer connected sockets, IP_PKTINFO/IP_RECVDSTADDR, ECN/CE via recvmsg cmsg, SO_BINDTODEVICE/IP_BOUND_IF) and SCM_RIGHTS fd passing (the FIPS native datagram API) need sendmsg/recvmsg. metadesk's own future UDP media path over fibers would hit the same wall.

What: add gof_recvfrom, gof_sendto, gof_recvmsg and gof_sendmsg to libfiber mirroring gof_read's park-on-EAGAIN/resume-on-readiness pattern (with the optional timeout_ms the connect/accept wrappers already take), cover them in libgo/fiber/tests (test_io.c / test_io_timeout.c), and document the UDP story in libgo/fiber/README.md 'Fiber-friendly I/O'.
acceptance_criteria: gof_recvfrom/gof_sendto/gof_recvmsg/gof_sendmsg exist, park the fiber instead of the worker, pass an epoll and a kqueue test, and are documented in the fiber README

description:
Why: docs/investigations/fips-rust-to-c-port-on-nostrc-2026-11-13.md (nostrc, branch feature/fips) re-verified metadesk against fips@6aa80504 (v0.6.0-dev) and found two drifts in the external FIPS runtime contract.

1. docs/metadesk-spec.md §2.2.1 still says 'Upstream FIPS v0.3.x / v0.4.x'; fips tags run through v0.5.3 and master is 0.6.0-dev. title: TLS stream SSL_write can raise SIGPIPE on Linux (OpenSSL socket BIO uses write(), no MSG_NOSIGNAL)
description: Why: plain TCP sends use MSG_NOSIGNAL on Linux (SO_NOSIGPIPE on macOS), so a peer that vanishes mid-send is EPIPE. TLS sends go through OpenSSL's socket BIO, which on Unix writes with write(): on Linux a vanished peer raises SIGPIPE. The host does not ignore SIGPIPE (only the client does), so a host serving TLS would be killed. Latent: the host only serves plain TCP today. Found during md-z6nw. What: in stream.c, give TLS streams a send path that cannot signal (custom BIO write via send(..., MSG_NOSIGNAL), or block SIGPIPE around SSL_write and consume it with sigtimedwait), plus a Linux test: TLS peer closes mid-stream without SIGPIPE ignored in a child process.
notes: Orchestrator 2026-11-19: host/main.c already sets signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) at :65 (install_signal_handlers) and :715; client/main.c:675 too (md-0w0). Verify which execution path (if any) lacks it before fixing; likely only library consumers outside metadesk-host/-client, where MSG_NOSIGNAL/SO_NOSIGPIPE can't cover OpenSSL's write path. May be invalid for the binaries.
close_reason: Invalid: no metadesk path creates a TLS MdStream. md_stream_connect_tls/md_stream_server_create_tls have no callers outside stream.c (md_stream_server_create passes NULL tls) and tests/test_stream.c; host serves plain TCP (host/main.c:1238 md_stream_server_create) and client connects plain (client/main.c:478). Even so SIGPIPE is ignored in every socket binary: host/main.c:65 and :727, mcp-proxy (host/mcp_proxy.c:521, same binary), client/main.c:697, test_stream.c:688 before any TLS test, plus other test mains. Library consumers: libmetadesk.so installs no headers or pkg-config, so there is no supported external consumer. Reopen if a TLS caller is added outside a SIGPIPE-ignoring main.

title: test_capture_dxgi_win: pointer cells flaky on the VM console (color shape not seen composited; idle_cells)
description: Why: while qualifying md-4dsa (2026-11-19) pristine master 140214f failed the --interactive DXGI test 6 of 30 console runs, interleaved with the branch (which failed it 2 of 30): 5x CHECK(hardware) (no colour shape ever matched as a composited DXGI pointer within the budget) and 1x CHECK(idle_cells == 2). close_reason: Fixed in 001f930 (branch fix/md-v9wt-dxgi-pointer-cells). Root cause: the test, not the backend. A shape change reaches DXGI as a pointer-only update before DWM repaints, so the image still holds the previous software cursor (erased 2-47 ms later). drain_to_idle phase-locks each change ~100 ms before the console's display power-off. When the power-off wins, DXGI reports the pointer hidden at 0,0, and the old 'any non-background pixel' software check took the stale mono cursor for a software color cursor, failing CHECK(hardware). The show_cursor-off single 150 ms wait was spoiled by the wake redraw. Now: positive pixel evidence (exact composite, or DWM's own rendering incl. its monochrome reduction of masked color); pointer-only proof by timestamp == LastMouseUpdateTime; show/hide and show_cursor-off repeat across display power changes via barriers; SKIP if every shape is a positively identified software cursor. title: nostr.c md_nostr_wait_history timeout steps with the wall clock (CLOCK_REALTIME condvar)
description: Why: md-5aua moved every metadesk deadline onto md_monotonic_ns() and converted the REALTIME condvar timeouts in mcp_bridge.c and mcp_proxy.c to md_cond_init_monotonic()/md_cond_timedwait_until() (src/core/md_time.h). md_nostr_wait_history in src/core/nostr.c (~line 692) still builds its deadline from clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME) against allowlist_cv's default clock. It was left alone because md-ip2k owns nostr.* concurrently. A wall-clock step back extends the history wait, and a step forward cuts it short. What: init allowlist_cv with md_cond_init_monotonic() (check every other wait on it, since all must then use the monotonic clock), compute deadline = md_monotonic_ns() + timeout, and wait with md_cond_timedwait_until. Run the nostr tests and the Nostr protocol review.
close_reason: f46d33a: allowlist_cv is monotonic (md_cond_init_monotonic); md_nostr_wait_history deadline = md_monotonic_ns() + timeout, md_cond_timedwait_until. No other relative-timeout waits in nostr.c. New HISTORY_WAITING test point; test_history_wait covers the bound, a Linux CLOCK_REALTIME step (old code fails), EOSE wake and stop wake. macOS + Linux full suite parallel/serial, ASan, TSan green.

title: MdStream connected flag races between concurrent send and recv on one stream
description: Why: the host sends video from the capture thread (md_stream_send under client_mu) while the main thread calls md_stream_recv on the same MdStream without that lock. stream.c reads s->connected in md_stream_send and writes s->connected=false in md_stream_recv on EOF/error (and vice versa), unsynchronized. TSan reproduced it in tests/test_capture_sync.c (md-ezto/md-pvlj) when the peer closed while a send was in flight: read at stream.c md_stream_send vs write at md_stream_recv. Benign-looking today (a bool), but it is a C data race and stats fields may share the pattern. What: make connected (and any shared stats) atomic or guard them with a stream-internal lock; add a TSan test doing concurrent send+recv with a peer close.
close_reason: Fixed in 8edf631: connected and the traffic counters are relaxed atomics. test_concurrent_send_recv_peer_close: TSan on Linux reports races in 3/3 runs on master's stream.c and is clean 10/10 after the fix; test_capture_sync is TSan-clean too. Follow-up: md-z6nw (TLS concurrent use).

title: Host capture restart does not refresh encoder size or input output bounds
description: Why: the host's capture watchdog recovers a broken stream with md_capture_stop + md_capture_start, and backends re-resolve the output there. DXGI re-reads the mode, rotation and, for --capture-output all, the set of outputs and their bounding rectangle, then republishes ctx->width/height and ctx->output_rect. But main.c sizes the encoder and copies md_capture_get_output_rect into MdInputConfig.output_* only once at startup. After a display mode change, rotation, re-arrangement or attach/detach, capture recovers, but changed-size frames no longer match the encoder, and input keeps targeting the old rectangle. Noted by the md-246 review; pre-existing for mode changes, more reachable with all-outputs mode. What: after a successful restart, re-read md_capture_get_size and md_capture_get_output_rect, then rebuild the encoder or end the session if the size changed, and update the input bounds under the input lock (or recreate the input context). Applies to macOS (md-xat) too.
close_reason: Fixed in 24bd5a4 (fix/host-ezto-pvlj): host/capture_sync reconciles every frame. On a size change it re-opens the encoder (md_encoder_resize, which forces an IDR); on a size or rect change it retargets input under client_mu (md_input_set_bounds). The capture thread owns the encoder, with keyframe/bitrate requests posted as atomics. Tests: test_capture_sync (mock restart, TCP e2e); real Sway/PipeWire mode change 1920x1080 -> 1280x720 and -> 1365x767 validated. Follow-ups: md-f1oo, md-383x, md-9sa6.

title: Windows host is not per-monitor DPI aware: UIA action coordinates are virtualized while capture/input use physical pixels
description: Why: md-w65 made DXGI publish the captured output rect (md_capture_get_output_rect) and SendInput normalise against the virtual desktop in physical pixels (win_dpi.h scopes the geometry queries per-monitor aware), so frame-relative client input is exact on any DPI layout. Agent actions and MCP clicks instead use UIA BoundingRectangle coordinates, which for a DPI-unaware process are DPI-virtualized on displays scaled above 100% (and per-monitor inconsistent on mixed DPI). md_input_execute_action converts those global points against the physical output rect, and the MCP legacy path normalises them against the physical virtual desktop, so on scaled displays agent clicks drift. What: declare the Windows host (and MCP) process per-monitor-aware v2 (application manifest, or SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext before any window/UIA/DXGI call), then verify UIA rects equal physical pixels on a scaled display. Not testable on the VM's 100% single output without changing its scaling.
close_reason: Fixed in a3b8a8a (branch fix/windows-m5x4-4dsa): md_win_dpi_process_init() (win_dpi.h, C-compatible) is the first statement of host main() -> per-monitor v2 (API, not manifest: meson Windows build blocked, manifest unverifiable). UIA walks also inside MdPhysicalPixels; DXGI init logs a non-per-monitor process. Coordinate chain all physical: UIA rects, DXGI output rect/all bounds, SendInput virtual desktop, md_input_execute_action inverse of md_input_map_to_output. Synthetic mixed-DPI tests (VM is 100%): DPI-virtualizing GetSystemMetrics/GetMonitorInfoW fakes, agent/MCP clicks exact on 100/125/150% outputs. Qualified: clang -Wall -Wextra -Werror, MSVC /W4 /WX (C++ and C incl. a main.c-shaped TU), session 0 (preset per-monitor v1 reported) and console (unaware -> v2). Real scaled display: md-74xp.

title: test_capture_dxgi_win: healthy-stream timing cell flaky on the VM console (AcquireNextFrame overruns its timeout)
description: Why: the --interactive 'healthy stream' cell (over < 100 ms past each get_frame timeout) fails intermittently on the Windows VM console on pristine master 7cb7ab5/2cb7117 as well as on md-w65 branches: e.g. 'timeout 250: frame after 465 ms' / 'IDLE after 610 ms' (master failed 1 of 3 runs, branch 2 of 3, same session, host idle). get_frame computes each AcquireNextFrame wait from the deadline, so AcquireNextFrame itself is blocking hundreds of ms past its timeout, most likely around the VM console display power transitions the test windows keep re-waking (see memory windows-vm-dxgi-pointer-facts-md-346). What: confirm the cause (log AcquireNextFrame entry/exit vs GUID_CONSOLE_DISPLAY_STATE changes), then either make the cell tolerate overruns that coincide with a display-state transition or keep the display awake differently; do not loosen the bound blindly.
close_reason: Fixed in 44adbd0. Root cause (traced AcquireNextFrame/Map vs GUID_CONSOLE_DISPLAY_STATE + 1 ms heartbeat): (1) VM console display power changes stall duplication (10188 calls: every >50 ms overrun overlapped a change; clean worst 24 ms); (2) on a loaded Mac host (load 30-60) the test process/vCPU is unscheduled 70-220 ms. Not DWM cadence, not budget. Fix: timing cells keep the 100 ms bound but time only calls with a steady display state and no scheduling gap >=50 ms, read after event barriers (posted-message ack, fresh heartbeat); others reported and repeated (<=40). Qualification: 31/31 console processes passed both timing cells first try plus MD_DXGI_HEALTHY_REPEAT=300 (1800 samples, worst 47 ms, 71 untimed: 69 display, 2 scheduling). Whole-test retry no longer needed for the timing cells; remaining whole-test flake is the pre-existing pointer cells (md-v9wt, master 6/30).

title: ScreenCaptureKit captures at point resolution on Retina (half-res frames)
description: Why: capture_screencapturekit.m sets SCStreamConfiguration width/height from SCDisplay.width/height, which are points. On the 3024x1964 built-in display, md-xat's smoke test captured 1512x982. What: capture at pixel size (points x the display's backing scale, e.g. CGDisplayModeGetPixelWidth) behind a config/bitrate decision, keeping ctx->output_rect in CG points. md_input_map_to_output already scales frame to output bounds, so input stays correct.
close_reason: SCK now captures backing pixels (3024x1964 on the 1512x982-pt panel); output_rect stays in points; mapping is covered by test_input Retina cases. Downscale option deliberately not added (md-n9p2). Restart size refresh is md-pvlj.

title: DXGI capture ignores output rotation (DXGI_OUTDUPL_DESC.Rotation)
description: Why: Desktop Duplication returns the desktop image in the output's native (unrotated) orientation; capture_dxgi.cpp copies it as-is and sizes frames from ModeDesc, so a portrait/rotated monitor streams sideways, and pointer positions/compositing would need the same transform. Pre-existing; noticed during md-346. What: read DXGI_OUTDUPL_DESC.Rotation, rotate on copy (CPU or a GPU pass) and report rotated dimensions; rotate pointer shape/position consistently.
close_reason: Committed on feat/windows-w65-dbg-246: rotated outputs are turned into a CPU frame in desktop orientation (MS sample/libwebrtc convention), pointer composited in desktop coordinates, output_rect/frame both desktop-oriented so input maps linearly. Synthetic per-pixel tests for all rotations + forced-rotation console cell on real frames.

title: DXGI capture ignores MdCaptureConfig.show_cursor (pointer never composited)
description: Why: Desktop Duplication returns the desktop image without the pointer; the pointer shape/position come separately (GetFramePointerShape, DXGI_OUTDUPL_FRAME_INFO.PointerPosition). capture_dxgi.cpp never reads them, so show_cursor=true (the md_capture_create default) is silently ignored on Windows, unlike SCK/PipeWire. Also found while doing md-7yc: pointer-only updates are now reported as IDLE (no image damage), which is right only while the pointer is not composited. What: either composite the pointer into the staging copy when config.show_cursor (and then treat pointer-only updates as damage), or document/report that the Windows backend cannot honour it. Also EnumOutputs(0) captures only the first output of the default adapter (no multi-monitor selection).
close_reason: DXGI composites the pointer when show_cursor (mono/color premultiplied/masked-color, hotspot, visibility, save-under; pointer-only updates are damage only with show_cursor); output selectable via MdCaptureConfig.output / --capture-output (index or device name, default primary, unknown fails init). Commit 4b39f44. Follow-ups md-w65, md-246, md-dbg, md-xat.

title: UBSan: signed left-shift overflow in fips_addr.c convert_bits (bech32)
description: Under -Db_sanitize=address,undefined, metadesk-host access add <npub> reports: src/core/fips_addr.c:162:20 'left shift of 830545893 by 5 places cannot be represented in type int' and :175:43 (pad path), via decode_npub -> md_fips_npub_to_pubkey_hex. acc is an int accumulator that is never masked; standard bech32 convert_bits masks acc to (from_bits+to_bits-1) bits or uses uint32_t. Results are currently correct on two's-complement but it is UB. Fix: uint32_t acc, mask after each step (acc &= (1u << (from_bits + to_bits - 1)) - 1). Found during md-6ns ASan e2e (pre-existing, out of scope).
close_reason: Fixed unsigned masked bech32 accumulator; added exact npub vectors and 90-character rejection coverage, enlarging decode scratch space for that boundary. macOS meson 32/32, macOS ASan+UBSan FIPS test clean (leak detection disabled), Linux VM full suite 33/33 at -j2. Baseline regression reproduces UBSan shift overflow. VM ~/wt-tiy removed. Local-only delivery; no push/merge.

description: md-6ns fixed stale session_accept/request replay from retaining relays (request_id correlation + host live/EOSE gate). deploy/containers/reference/validate-client.py still starts a fresh relay per cell (fresh_relay) to avoid it. Reuse one retaining fixture relay across cells (or add a dedicated repeat cell) and assert the second negotiation succeeds and logs 'ignoring session request from relay history' / 'ignoring session_accept not answering the current request'. Needs rootless Podman images (not present on the Linux VM at md-6ns time). See client-validation.md Medium F.

Rootless Podman 73/73, 81 s. Commits 6521e58..fc853b3 on feat/client-cdz-rnc.

title: MCP: notify tools/list_changed when a live principal's grant changes
description: Follow-up to md-5km. tools/list is filtered per principal and every tools/call is re-gated on the current host-allowlist grant, so correctness holds. But metadesk does not declare tools.listChanged or send notifications/tools/list_changed. A client that cached tools/list does not learn that a grant was narrowed (agent+input -> agent) until a call returns isError, or that it was widened until it re-lists. Design: declare capabilities.tools.listChanged; on each accepted allowlist version (md_nostr_allowlist_wait_change, event-driven, never a timer), recompute each live SSE client's grant (store per-SseClient caps in mcp_http.c), and send notifications/tools/list_changed to just the clients whose action visibility changed (drop the stream if it lost agent, as today). Needs a per-client SSE send (today md_mcp_http_send_sse broadcasts) and an ACL change hook from host_mcp_acl to the HTTP transport. Tests: private-relay e2e publishing v1:agent,input -> v1:agent and asserting list_changed on the proxy's SSE stream, with no notification to static/bearer clients.
close_reason: Implemented in b044f56 (branch feat/md-ht7-tools-list-changed, not pushed/merged). Event-driven list_changed via host_mcp_acl_watch + MdMcpHttpConfig.nip98_grant_watch; targeted per-stream tool-set comparison; revocation closes streams on change; tools.listChanged advertised while a feed is registered; teardown unregisters first. Gates: macOS meson test 37/37 (nip46/nip55l/nip5f), macOS ASan MCP 6/6; Linux -j2 38 OK/1 skip(access e2e opt-in), serial same; Linux ASan+UBSan+LSan MCP 6/6. Protocol review: no polling/timeouts/new REQ; one test smell fixed (EOF vs timeout).

title: Host/client stdout is block-buffered without a TTY (container logs delayed until exit)
description: Found by md-ah9.11. metadesk-host and metadesk-client printf progress (e.g. 'nostr bridge ready, waiting for session requests', stats) to stdout; under podman/docker without -t, stdout is a pipe and block-buffered, so 'podman logs' shows these lines only at exit. The md-ah9.11 driver first started clients against a host that had already hit its 60 s request timeout. tests/access_session_e2e.py and validate-client.py work around it with stdbuf -oL -eL. Containers, systemd and supervisors all see delayed or lost readiness lines.
acceptance_criteria: Both binaries line-buffer (setvbuf) or flush progress output; container logs show readiness without stdbuf
close_reason: Client line-buffers stdout at startup; host only in video mode after the MCP return (MCP stdio uses write(2) on fd 1). stdbuf removed from validate-client.py and access_session_e2e; container host readiness logged while running; new tests/test_client_startup.py. macOS 31/31, Linux 36+1skip -j2 and serial, e2e opt-in OK, container 44/44.

title: GUI client display authorization fails open and is unobservable
description: Found by md-ah9.11 (container GUI cells). Without a granted display the GUI client never fails: (1) default env: SDL 2.30 silently selects its 'offscreen' EGL driver (Mesa present), the client reports displayed=N frames and exits 0 although nothing is visible; (2) SDL_VIDEODRIVER=wayland with no socket: 'render: SDL_Init failed: wayland not available', 'WARNING: SDL2 renderer unavailable, decode-only mode', continues decode-only, exit 0. The client never logs the selected SDL video driver or decoded frame dimensions, so operators cannot tell a visible session from an invisible one. Also: SDL's default opengl renderer segfaults on Wayland when libOpenGL.so.0 is absent (fixed in Dockerfile.client gui by libopengl0); a GLES2 fallback/hint in the client would be more robust. No src/ changes made by md-ah9.11.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit GUI mode fails closed (or an opt-in --require-display) when no real display driver is available; the client logs the SDL video driver/renderer and decoded dimensions
close_reason: GUI mode checks display at startup and refuses offscreen/dummy/evdev or SDL_Init failure with exit 1 before signer/session work; window failure fatal; logs SDL video driver, renderer, decoded frame size. Container cells: granted wayland PASS, both no-display cells clean refusals. GLES2 fallback split to md-rnc.

title: UIA subtree prefetch is width-unbounded: very wide non-virtualised lists overfetch
description: Why: md-cw8 walks each top-level window with one IUIAutomationCacheRequest (TreeScope_Subtree) round trip. UIA cannot bound a subtree cache fetch by depth or width (IUIAutomation2 TransactionTimeout is per provider call: even 1 ms did not fail a 150 ms subtree fetch), so nodes beyond MD_UIA_MAX_CHILDREN=256 / MD_UIA_MAX_DEPTH=32 are fetched and then dropped. Measured on the Win11 ARM64 VM (interactive): a fixture with a 5000-item Win32 LISTBOX took 1.2-1.6 s cached vs 0.6-0.8 s with the old capped uncached walk. A Win32 virtual ListView exposing ~100k items through the MSAA proxy could take tens of seconds while holding the backend tree lock. What: find a width bound that keeps most of the speedup. Measured alternatives: bounded GetFirst/NextSiblingElementBuildCache navigation (2 round trips per node, exact old semantics) is only ~1.5-2x faster than uncached on the desktop but is safe on wide lists (5000 items: 447 ms vs 829 ms uncached). A per-level Element|Children fetch is width-unbounded too. Options: (a) remember top-level windows (by RuntimeId) whose last subtree fetch exceeded the caps and walk those with bounded navigation; the first walk still pays. (b) identify Win32 item containers (ClassName SysListView32/ListBox/ComboLBox/SysTreeView32) and walk them with bounded navigation, but excluding their items from the subtree filter promotes descendants and breaks grouped lists, so this needs care. Measure with tests/test_uia_walk_equiv.cpp built with -DFIXTURE_LIST_ITEMS=5000 (see tools/win/README.md).
acceptance_criteria: test_uia_walk_equiv stays green (output identical); the 5000-item fixture walk is no slower than the uncached reference; the desktop walk keeps >=2.5x over uncached.
close_reason: 9ea9b1b: Win32 wide-container scan (>1024 items) routes those top-level windows to bounded BuildCache navigation; others keep the single subtree fetch. 5000-item fixture 1370->400 ms (uncached 760), 100k virtual ListView 20.6 s->650 ms (uncached 1310), desktop 2.7-2.9x (scan 0.3 ms). test_uia_walk_equiv byte-identical across all tiers.

title: Verify uinput udev-settle wait (uinput_dev_create) on a disposable desktop
description: 5bad2ce replaced the post-UI_DEV_CREATE 5 ms sleep in src/core/input_uinput.c with a libudev monitor wait: the monitor is enabled before UI_DEV_CREATE, and the code then waits for udev's 'add' of the eventN child of UI_GET_SYSNAME. The wait is bounded at 1 s, its deadline is also checked while draining, and it is skipped when udevd is inactive. It is compile-checked on Linux (gcc, ASan) and Oracle-reviewed, but it has NOT been exercised at runtime: md-2ml forbids creating uinput devices on the shared VM's live desktop, and a container shares the host kernel, so its devices reach the live GNOME session. Needs a disposable desktop (a separate throwaway VM) with MD_INPUT_LIVE_TESTS=1. Check (a) that the wait returns on the add event within milliseconds and does not log the 'udev did not announce' warning, (b) that the no-udevd path skips immediately, and (c) that the first injected key after md_input_create is delivered.
acceptance_criteria: Live run on a disposable desktop: both devices settle without the timeout warning; test_input live cells pass; the timing of the first post-create event is recorded.

title: nostrc pool: CLOSED-reason-aware re-REQ backoff (permanent refusals re-REQ every 200ms)
description: nostrc libnostr/src/simplepool.c pool_reconcile_subs re-fires any pruned subscription at the worker cadence (<=200ms) regardless of CLOSED reason. metadesk relies on it to recover after CLOSED auth-required + NIP-42 AUTH (md-ah9.3 MCP host allowlist, video ACL), but for blocked:/restricted: it is an unbounded re-REQ loop against a refusing relay. metadesk stays fail-closed. Found by the md-ah9.3 diff-scoped nostr-protocol-smells review. Fix upstream: auth-required -> re-REQ after successful AUTH; other reasons -> exponential backoff; blocked/restricted -> stop until reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: private-relay test: CLOSED blocked: yields bounded REQ count over a fixed number of reconnect events; auth-required recovers after AUTH
notes: Overlaps nostrc-7i6w scope item 4 (pool recovery without timer-driven pool_reconcile_subs re-firing). Fold into that nostrc work.

title: Stream/agent tests use fixed TCP ports (17700, 17820-17883 scan)
description: Found during md-e65. tests/test_stream.c binds fixed TEST_PORT 17700 and tests/test_agent.c test_format_aware_updates scans 17820..17883 because md_stream_server_create cannot report the port chosen by a port-0 bind. Two checkouts running the suite concurrently on the shared Linux VM (sibling agents do this routinely), or any unrelated listener, can collide: the same failure class as md-e65, where a held 18712 made test_mcp_http cascade into 12 failures. Fix the same way as md-e65: add an additive test-only accessor to report the bound port (getsockname after bind to :0), switch both tests to ephemeral ports, and fail on the first broken precondition. Production bind semantics must not change.
acceptance_criteria: No fixed or scanned port ranges in test_stream or test_agent; both tests pass while a foreign listener holds 17700 and 17820; production md_stream_server_create(port>0) behaviour unchanged.
close_reason: Use existing bound-port accessor with port 0 in stream/agent cases; fail-first setup; Linux collision witness passes with 17700/17820 held; full suites pass parallel and serial.

title: Qualify Compose reconciliation for the rootless mesh namespace holder
description: md-ah9.5 qualifies rootless Podman 4.9.3 API + standalone Docker Compose 5.5.1 using two-step up -d --no-recreate netns, then up -d --no-recreate. A plain second up -d tried to recreate unchanged ah9-5-netns; Podman refused removal because mesh depended on it and Compose left a temporary renamed holder. Cleaned only task containers and successfully reran with --no-recreate. Required mesh and agent restarts pass twice with stable holder inode; reconciliation/recreation is a separate unsupported path. Follow up by qualifying a Compose/Podman pairing that can safely reconcile this shared-userns/netns topology, or diagnose this API behavior. Do not restart the live desktop. See deploy/containers/reference/mesh-validation.md.
close_reason: Root cause: Podman <5.4 compat API reports NetworkID as network name, so Compose 5.5.1 always saw the networks:-attached holder as diverged (stopped it, failed removal, consumers lost underlay). Fix 90b7ca9: holder owned by Podman via mesh-netns.sh; consumers join container:ah9-5-netns; plain up -d idempotent. Qualified live (real fipsd mesh): repeat up -d no-op, consumer edit / --force-recreate keep holder, safety refusals and recovery. Podman>=5.4 requalification: md-czf.

title: UIA tree walk is ~3-5 ms/node: batch property reads with IUIAutomationCacheRequest
description:
Why: the first interactive Windows walk (Win11 ARM64 UTM VM) took 729-1155 ms for 250 nodes. a11y_uia.cpp walk_element() makes several cross-process COM calls per element (get_CurrentControlType, get_CurrentName, state properties, get_CurrentBoundingRectangle, runtime id, plus TreeWalker GetFirstChild/GetNextSibling). A real desktop with a browser or IDE open is thousands of nodes -> multi-second snapshots. Since md-ayo, walks happen only on reads (lazy MCP snapshot), not per event, so this is latency for agent reads rather than CPU burn — hence P3.

What: build one IUIAutomationCacheRequest with the properties walk_element needs (ControlType, Name, BoundingRectangle, IsEnabled, HasKeyboardFocus, IsOffscreen, toggle/selection/expand states as used by extract_states, RuntimeId) and TreeScope_Subtree (or Element+Children per level), then use FindAllBuildCache / GetCachedChildren and get_Cached* accessors. Keep the existing MAX_DEPTH/MAX_CHILDREN bounds. title: test_sse_stalled_client flaky under parallel test execution
description:
Why: tests/test_mcp_http.c test_sse_stalled_client (added in md-ed7, commit e9dfcc5/01291fe) fails or times out when the MCP suites are run in parallel on a loaded host (observed during md-ayo verification: 4 failures + 1 suite timeout in a parallel 10x repeat; assertions around tests/test_mcp_http.c:610/614/632). The same tests pass 10/10 when run serially. The test fills a kernel socket buffer to simulate a stalled SSE reader and asserts the stalled client is dropped within sse_write_timeout_ms while a healthy client keeps receiving; under CPU contention the timing window and the buffer-fill heuristics become scheduling-dependent.

What: make the test deterministic rather than timing-based — e.g. use a tiny SO_SNDBUF / SO_RCVBUF on the stalled client's socket pair so the buffer fills with a known small number of bytes, drive the write deadline with an injectable clock or a very short timeout plus a generous assertion window, and wait on observable state (client count drops; healthy client receives event N) with latch_wait instead of elapsed-time bounds. Also consider marking the HTTP suite is_parallel: false in meson.build as a stopgap if it remains sensitive. Logs from the failing run were under /tmp/md-ayo-*.log on the dev host (ephemeral).
acceptance_criteria: MCP HTTP suite passes 20/20 when the four MCP suites are run concurrently (meson test --num-processes 4 looped) on the dev host; no wall-clock bounds in test_sse_stalled_client.
close_reason: Merged to master as 837f3b1 (31c8256, 5a8d461). test_sse_stalled_client is state-based: pre-connect SO_RCVBUF on clients, sse_sndbuf test knob (SSE sockets only, 0 = untouched) bounds server-side buffering so all stalled clients overflow on the first broadcast; broadcast-until-count==1 with 1024-frame cap; 5->1 within one write asserted via count snapshots; single readiness probe; concurrent healthy reader terminated by sentinel; EOF confirmation 2s each. Remaining md_now_ms pass/fail bounds removed from HTTP/stdio tests; stdio memcmp fixed (json+queued, non-uniform payload). Verified: 22/22, 20x --num-processes 4 (80/80), 20x HTTP under 4 CPU burners (20/20), +3x parallel on merge. macOS only; Linux buffer accounting reasoned, not run.

title: MCP bridge shutdown can block on a stuck transport write inside the a11y change callback
description:
Why: after md-6h0, md_mcp_bridge_destroy() first calls md_a11y_unsubscribe_changes(), which waits for any in-flight md_mcp_a11y_change_cb to return (src/core/a11y.c change_clear_and_drain). That callback calls md_mcp_notify_tree_changed(server) -> server write_fn -> md_mcp_http_write / md_mcp_stdio_write. If the SSE client has stalled, or stdout is a full pipe whose reader is gone (SIGPIPE ignored), the write blocks, the drain never completes, and destroy never reaches md_mcp_http_destroy / md_mcp_stdio_destroy — the only things that would unblock the write. Pre-existing class of problem (a blocked write also wedged the event thread before md-6h0); the drain just makes it surface at shutdown. Found in code review of fix/md-6h0-a11y-unsubscribe.

What: give the bridge a shutdown sequence that cannot wedge: (a) add md_mcp_server_detach_transport() (or make write_fn a no-op) so notifications become drop-on-floor once shutdown starts; call it BEFORE the drain, then destroy transports, then drain, then free; or (b) make the transport writes non-blocking / bounded (poll with timeout, drop notification on timeout) so a callback can never block indefinitely. Prefer (b) for the SSE path since a stalled client should never stall the host regardless of shutdown. Test: fake write_fn that blocks on a semaphore; call md_mcp_bridge_destroy from another thread; assert it returns within a bound after the transport is torn down.
acceptance_criteria: md_mcp_bridge_destroy returns within a bounded time with a change callback blocked in write_fn; no UAF (run under ASan); existing tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to master as 9cb539f (d216ead, e9dfcc5, 01291fe). Bounded SSE/POST/stdio writes (SO_SNDTIMEO, poll-deadline helper in io_util), server quiesce + sink_mu before a11y drain, SSE admission fix. 22/22 unit, MCP suites x10, ASan clean on macOS

title: MCP read tools: serve from cached a11y snapshot instead of full walk per call
description:
Why: the md-n68 read tools (metadesk_find/subtree/node/focused/windows in src/core/mcp_tools.c) each perform a fresh md_a11y_walk() — a full desktop traversal (thousands of D-Bus round trips on AT-SPI) — even for single-node lookups. An agent doing find -> node -> subtree -> click walks the desktop four times for an unchanged UI. MdAgent already keeps cached_tree for target resolution (src/core/agent.c), and the bridge registers a change subscription (src/core/mcp_bridge.c) that could invalidate a shared snapshot.

What: introduce one bridge-owned snapshot (mutex-protected) shared by the agent's target resolution, the ui-tree resource, and the read tools; invalidate it after actions and on md_mcp_a11y_change_cb; refresh lazily on next read. Keep md_a11y_walk semantics for the stream path unchanged. Also fold in the smaller review nits from md-n68: build compact find output into one StrBuf instead of a temporary cJSON string array; make read-tool validation errors name the offending field (as extract_args does for action tools); consider strcasecmp/strcasestr vs the hand-rolled equal_ci/contains_ci (keep hand-rolled only if MSVC portability is the reason, and say so in a comment).

Depends on md-1kg (subscribe_changes) for correct invalidation on Linux/macOS/Windows; without it, snapshot staleness is bounded only by post-action invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: Read tools and ui-tree resource share one snapshot; a find->node->subtree sequence on an unchanged UI performs one walk (assert via a counting fake backend in test_mcp); snapshot invalidated after any action tool and on change callback; all tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to master as 8129758 (commits 9864e03,12be22b for md-qqz; a365ef0,b1b665f for md-52m); 22/22 tests

title: nostrc/libgo: atomic snapshot-swap helper (watch/ArcSwap analogue) over refptr
description:
Target repo: nostrc (libgo). Filed here because metadesk is the consumer; see docs/investigations/fips-rust-to-c-port-on-nostrc-2026-11-13.md §5.3 in nostrc (branch feature/fips).

Why: libgo has channels, select, contexts, wait groups and refptr, but no primitive for 'many readers take a consistent snapshot of a value a writer replaces wholesale'. Rust code of the kind metadesk may port or mirror uses tokio::sync::watch (20 sites in fips) and arc_swap::ArcSwap (58 sites) for exactly this: config reload, peer tables, routing snapshots read on hot paths without a lock. Today the C options are a mutex around a pointer (contention on hot reads) or a hand-rolled _Atomic pointer with ad-hoc refcount discipline per call site.

What: add a small libgo type (e.g. GoSwap) holding an _Atomic(void*) to a refptr-managed value with go_swap_load (retain + return), go_swap_store (publish new, release old), and optionally a GoChannel notification for watch-style wakeups; tests under libgo/tests including a TSan run; document in libgo/LIBGO.md.
acceptance_criteria: GoSwap (or equivalent) lands in libgo with load/store semantics that never free a value a reader still holds, a stress test passes under TSan, and LIBGO.md documents it

title: DXGI size cap: qualify on a hardware GPU and real multi-monitor/rotated displays
description: md-jie5 added the GPU area-averaging downscale before the DXGI staging copy. It was qualified only on the VM's Microsoft Basic Render Driver (software rasterizer, one 1024x768 output; rotation and multi-output forced or synthetic). Still to check on real hardware: (1) per-frame cost of scaler_run + copy + map on a discrete or integrated GPU (WARP: ~3 ms 1024x768->640x480, ~9 ms 4K->1080p); (2) whether the acquired desktop texture is bindable as an SRV (direct path) or takes the copy_source fallback; (3) 'all' under a cap across two adapters, and a physically rotated monitor; (4) a hardware color pointer drawn scaled on a HiDPI display.
