title: capture_sync: bound packet-run history below 2^31 sequences
description: Why: host_capture_sync_map_point compares sequences modulo 2^32 (seq_at_or_after). A single run of one geometry that lasts more than 2^31 packets (about 414 days at 60 fps) makes recent current-geometry points compare as before the run, so they are dropped. md-383x's first_seq had the same limit. What: when the counter gets 2^30 or more ahead of the oldest retained run start, advance that run start or trim old runs, so that held distances stay below 2^31. Found in the md-f7uc review.

title: Hardware-verify per-frame encoder tags on AMF and NVENC (Windows)
description: Why: md-f7uc carries a per-frame geometry tag through the encoder by matching packet pts to an in-flight (pts, tag) table (src/core/encode.c). It relies on the codec returning each frame's pts on its packet. That held on h264_videotoolbox (macOS) and libx264 (Linux), but h264_amf and h264_nvenc were not run. On macOS, VideoToolbox emitted every packet within its own submit in the tests, so a genuinely late emission was only exercised by the mock delay line in test_capture_sync. What: run test_encode's test_tags_follow_frames on the Windows VM with AMF/NVENC hardware (or note that no hardware encoder is available there), confirm that untagged == 0, and record whether any packets were emitted late.

title: SCK: verify system-stop path on real hardware (display unplug / TCC revoke)
description: md-2p10 added an SCStreamDelegate that marks the SCK stream broken on stream:didStopWithError: (get_frame -> MD_CAPTURE_ERROR, host watchdog restart). Covered by tests/test_capture_sck.m via a test seam only; it was not exercised against a real system stop. Manually: run metadesk-host capturing an external display, unplug it (expect 'capture stream ended by ScreenCaptureKit (SCStreamErrorDomain <code> ...)' then a watchdog restart onto a remaining display or a clean failure); and revoke Screen Recording mid-stream (expect the 'Screen Recording permission revoked' line). Record which SCStreamErrorCode each case actually delivers and adjust the sck_stop_errors table if needed.

title: Input frame tag: attribute async-encoder frames to geometry by capture frame, not change time
description: Why: md-383x attributes MD_PKT_INPUT points to a geometry by the frame-channel sequence the host counter stood at when the geometry changed (capture_sync first_seq). On a rectangle-only change (same frame size, e.g. display rearranged) the encoder is not re-opened, so an asynchronous encoder (h264_videotoolbox, h264_amf) can still emit a packet for a frame captured under the OLD rectangle after first_seq; clicks on that frame are then treated as current and injected against the new rectangle. Window: encoder pipeline depth (~1 frame), same-size rect changes only. What: record the capture frame.seq (encoder pts) of the first frame submitted at the new geometry, and set first_seq in host on_encoded when pkt->pts reaches it (needs host/main.c on_encoded + capture_sync hook), or force a keyframe/flush on rect-only changes. Documented as a residual in docs/metadesk-spec.md section 9.3.
close_reason: Fixed in ae137a6. Packets are attributed to the geometry their capture frame was taken under. The capture thread tags each frame with its geometry generation, md_encoder_submit_tagged carries the tag to the packet via an in-flight (pts, tag) table, and host on_encoded reports (tag, seq) runs to capture_sync. map_point resolves a point's frame_pkt_seq to its run's geometry. Sync and async encoders are handled alike. Tests use a mock async delay line, the real codec on VT/x264, and an e2e rect-only phase. Spec §9.3 is updated. Follow-ups: md-32a9 (AMF/NVENC hardware check), md-wc00 (2^31 history bound).

title: PipeWire: support the capture size cap (MdCaptureConfig.max_width/max_height)
description: Why: md-n9p2 added a platform-neutral capture size cap (host --capture-max-size WxH, md_capture_fit_size). PipeWire rejects it in pw_backend_init (and the host rejects the flag on Linux): mutter/xdp monitor streams offer a fixed size, so format negotiation cannot shrink them. What: scale SHM/DMA-BUF frames before the encoder, e.g. libswscale on the SHM path or a VAAPI/GL scale on DMA-BUF, at md_capture_fit_size of the negotiated size. Publish that size and keep output_rect unset/unchanged (input scales via screen_* vs output_*). Then drop the init rejection and host #ifdef, and add test_capture coverage.
close_reason: Implemented in 3fce48e (branch feat/md-awgm-pipewire-size-cap, rebased on ad1fcf5). Negotiation measured infeasible: offering only sizes <= cap fails xdpw 0.7.1's link ('no more input formats', zero frames). Shipped consumer-side CPU box scale in pw_get_frame (md_capture_scale_frame), PW buffer borrowed until release_frame, fitted size published via wait_size; host gate removed. Real backend (Sway/xdpw, renderD128): 1280x0 -> 1280x720, 1000x1000 -> 1000x563, 64x0 -> 64x36, all gates 0 failures; capped latency p50 ~2.0-2.2 ms vs 0.05 ms native; box ~2 ms vs bilinear ~4 ms at 1280x720. macOS 37/37, Linux 36/36 parallel+serial.

title: DXGI: support the capture size cap (MdCaptureConfig.max_width/max_height)
description: Why: md-n9p2 added a platform-neutral capture size cap (host --capture-max-size WxH, md_capture_fit_size) for bandwidth-limited sessions. SCK scales in hardware. DXGI rejects it in dxgi_init (and the host rejects the flag on Windows) because frames are the zero-copy mapped staging copy of the desktop image. What: add a GPU downscale before staging (ID3D11VideoProcessor, or a shader blit into a smaller render target then CopyResource to a capped-size staging texture), including the rotated/'all' canvas paths. Then publish width/height as the capped size, keep output_rect physical (input maps unchanged, as md_input_map_to_output scales), drop the init rejection and the host #ifdef, and extend tests/test_capture_dxgi_win.cpp.
close_reason: Implemented in ebc99d7 (feat/md-jie5-dxgi-size-cap): GPU area-averaging pixel shader per output before the staging copy; FrameScale maps unscaled layout/pointer; rotation and 'all' via CPU over scaled copies; pointer composited at scaled position with scaled shape (color area-averaged, mono/masked point-sampled); zero-copy kept for unrotated single output; host gate lifted on Windows. Qualified: clang -Werror + MSVC /W4 /WX (backend and test TU), fxc /WX, session 0 4/4, console 6/6 first try, macOS meson 36/36.

title: MdStream: concurrent send+recv is unsafe on TLS streams (one SSL object, two threads)
description: Why: the host sends from its capture thread and receives on the main thread on one MdStream (md-9sa6 made connected and the counters atomic). That is safe for plaintext TCP, the only thing the host uses today: md_stream_server_create, and server_create_tls/connect_tls have no callers outside stream.c and tests. With TLS, SSL_write and SSL_read would run concurrently on the same SSL*, which OpenSSL does not allow. What: if the host ever serves TLS, serialise SSL_read/SSL_write with a stream-internal lock (careful: a blocking read must not hold it across poll), or document and enforce single-threaded use for TLS streams.
close_reason: 019dc67: TLS sockets non-blocking after handshake; per-stream ssl_mu around each SSL_read/SSL_write + SSL_get_error, released before poll() on WANT_*; plain TCP unchanged. test_tls_concurrent_duplex + TLS peer-close; Linux SSL-call overlap counter fails the old code. TSan 10/10 clean, ASan clean, full suites green.

title: Input events sent across a mid-stream resize are mapped against the new frame size
description: Why: md-ezto/md-pvlj re-open the encoder and retarget input on a capture size change; the wire carries no frame size (only the H.264 SPS does) and MD_PKT_INPUT carries only frame-relative x/y. Points the client sent before it decoded the new IDR (at most ~1 RTT) are interpreted by the host against the new frame size, so a click in that window can land scaled/offset. Documented in docs/metadesk-spec.md section 9.3. What (if it matters in practice): tag input events with the frame size (or a geometry generation) they were computed against and have the host scale or drop mismatched ones; needs a protocol version bump per spec section 3.
close_reason: Fixed: MD_PKT_INPUT carries an 8-byte frame tag (decoded size + video packet sequence); host attributes points by sequence to the geometry the frame was sent under, uses as-is / rescales (same rect) / drops. Client tags the presented frame and pumps input before each decode. Unit sweep + e2e resize-window test + dispatch test; macOS 36/36, Linux 36/36 parallel+serial, ASan/TSan clean. Commit 99c0b6c. Follow-up md-f7uc.

title: SCK: republish output_rect when the captured display moves without a capture restart
description: Why: md-ezto/md-pvlj made the host reconcile input bounds against md_capture_get_output_rect() on every captured frame (src/host/capture_sync.c), so any backend that republishes ctx->output_rect is picked up by the next frame. ScreenCaptureKit sets output_rect only in sck_start from CGDisplayBounds, so rearranging displays (or a main-display change that moves the CG origin) while a stream keeps running leaves the published rect, and therefore clicks, stale until a watchdog restart. What: in capture_screencapturekit.m, register CGDisplayRegisterReconfigurationCallback (or observe NSApplicationDidChangeScreenParametersNotification) and republish ctx->output_rect for the captured display ID, writing it so the capture thread's per-frame read is not torn (publish under the frame lock or via a seqlock). Left to the SCK owners (md-txsc/md-6c4f in flight); host side needs no change.
close_reason: c23ecf8 on feat/sck-f1oo-n9p2. SCK follows per-frame ScreenRect/ScaleFactor attachments (CGDisplayBounds per frame before 13.1). On change it re-reads CGDisplayBounds, and updateConfiguration runs on a pixel-size change, dropping letterboxed old-size frames until the new size. The rect and size are published in get_frame (consumer thread, frame_lock), so they are never torn. A failed reconfigure marks the stream broken, which triggers a watchdog restart. CGDisplayRegisterReconfigurationCallback is not used (event-thread only; host has no run loop). Tests: test_capture_sync republish-without-restart, macOS + Linux 36/36. A real display move was not triggerable here (single built-in display, no-op CG config rejected); updateConfiguration mid-stream behaviour was verified in a probe. Follow-up md-2p10.

title: Allowlist readiness: tell stale vs post-AUTH auth-required CLOSED apart (needs nostrc frame order)
description: Follow-up from md-ip2k protocol review. auth_path_open() keeps an accepted NIP-42 AUTH as an open path, because CLOSED notifications reach metadesk via the nostrc pool worker queue while OK arrives on the reader thread, so a stale auth-required CLOSED can be observed after OK true; treating it as terminal would spuriously close held MCP SSE streams on every auth-relay reconnect. Consequence: a relay that accepts our AUTH but keeps answering auth-required: (instead of restricted:) leaves readiness UNKNOWN and live-list streams held (bounded only by SSE-slot eviction). Same root cause: a CLOSED in flight at disconnect can be applied to the next connection until its next boundary (spurious FAILED, self-correcting). Fix needs ordering info from nostrc (e.g. a per-relay receive sequence passed to subscription/OK callbacks), then: auth-required CLOSED whose frame is newer than OK true => refused. Optional: use NIP-11 limitation.auth_required to classify auth-required without a challenge. Related: md-odg / nostrc-7i6w (re-REQ every ~200ms after CLOSED).

title: Optional capture downscale (e.g. macOS point resolution) for bandwidth-limited sessions
description: Why: md-txsc made SCK capture at backing pixels (3024x1964 instead of 1512x982 on a Retina MacBook). That is 4x the pixels to encode. We deliberately added no knob there: only host/main.c could expose it (owned by md-pvlj at the time), a config field with no caller would be dead code, and DXGI already captures physical pixels, so native is the cross-platform default. Bandwidth is governed by the bitrate controller. What: if sessions need it, add a platform-neutral MdCaptureConfig cap (e.g. max_width/max_height or a scale divisor; 0 = native) plus a host flag. SCK implements it for free via SCStreamConfiguration.width/height (hardware scaling). DXGI and PipeWire would need an encoder-side scaler. Input stays correct with no change, because md_input_map_to_output scales frame->output from the two sizes.
close_reason: c23ecf8. MdCaptureConfig.max_width/max_height + md_capture_fit_size (fit, keep aspect, never upscale) + host --capture-max-size WxH + capture_frame MAX_WxH. SCK applies it in hardware through SCStreamConfiguration. Smoke: 3024x1964 native, 1512x982 at the 1512x982 cap, 1078x700 at 0x700, with rect 1512x982 pts. SCK content covers the rounded size to within 0.25px. Input is unchanged; proof is in test_capture_sync capped test. DXGI/PipeWire reject it in init and host parse; follow-ups md-jie5 (DXGI), md-awgm (PipeWire).

title: Host input bounds go stale when the captured display moves or capture restarts
description: Why: md-xat copies md_capture_get_output_rect() into MdInputConfig once, at input creation in host/main.c. A watchdog capture restart republishes ctx->output_rect, and a display rearrangement changes CGDisplayBounds, but input keeps the old bounds, so clicks land offset. What: refresh the input's output bounds after a capture (re)start or on CGDisplayRegisterReconfigurationCallback, e.g. a md_input_set_output_rect setter. This is shared with DXGI (md-w65).
close_reason: Fixed in 24bd5a4 with md-pvlj: input bounds are refreshed from md_capture_get_output_rect on every frame after any restart or republish (md_input_set_bounds under the host input lock). An SCK reconfiguration callback that republishes the rect without a restart is filed as md-f1oo, for the SCK owners.

title: SCK MdFrame.timestamp_ns is not on CLOCK_MONOTONIC
description: Why: capture.h documents timestamp_ns as a monotonic capture timestamp. The SCK backend sets it from CMSampleBuffer PTS seconds (host-time clock). tools/capture_frame, which subtracts it from CLOCK_MONOTONIC, reported a latency of ~1.79e12 ms during the md-xat smoke test. What: convert the PTS to the clock the HAL promises, e.g. via CMClockConvertHostTimeToSystemUnits / mach time, or document the clock. Then check the consumers (encoder pts, stats).
close_reason: PTS (host clock / mach_absolute_time) is rebased per frame onto md_capture_clock_ns (CLOCK_MONOTONIC via clock_gettime_nsec_np), clamped and non-decreasing; test_frame_clock covers it. capture_frame latency is now 0.01-65 ms. The root of the bogus number, libnsync shadowing clock_gettime, is filed as md-5aua.

title: MCP: end held live SSE streams when every relay terminally CLOSED the allowlist REQ
description: Follow-up from md-554 protocol review. host_mcp_acl_grant() answers MD_MCP_GRANT_UNKNOWN (hold open SSE streams) whenever readiness is FAILED, whatever the cause: all relays DISCONNECTED/BACKOFF (transient: the pool reconnects and re-REQs, EOSE releases the hold) OR every relay answered CLOSED. A non-auth CLOSED (e.g. 'restricted:') is terminal until the next reconnect, so no EOSE will come and held streams stay open and silent until shutdown, host-role change, or SSE-capacity eviction by a static/bearer newcomer. No data leaks (POSTs still 401). Fix: per-relay terminal-CLOSED bit in nostr.c (set on non-auth-required CLOSED, cleared on the next connection-state transition); md_nostr_granted_capabilities_known() reports known=true (deny -> close) when every relay is terminal-CLOSED, unknown while any relay is disconnected/backoff/awaiting AUTH. Touches src/core/nostr.c, tests/test_nostr.c (acl fixture 'closed' op), docs/mcp-auth.md.
close_reason: Fixed in 775081d (branch fix/md-ip2k-terminal-closed, not merged). CLOSED classified by NIP-01 prefix: rate-limited: and auth-required:-with-AUTH-path transient (UNKNOWN, held); auth-required: without AUTH path and every other/no prefix refused. All relays refused => FAILED, now known (deny): held MCP streams close on that wake-up, 401, host log names relay+reason. UNKNOWN now also covers all-down (was FAILED); edit/snapshot waits re-pointed to pending so they still fail fast. Event-driven (CLOSED/EOSE/AUTH/OK/state), no timers; nostrc untouched. Gates: macOS meson test 38/38 (nip46/55l/5f), macOS ASan+UBSan MCP/nostr 9/9, Linux VM 39 OK/1 opt-in skip parallel -j2 and serial, Linux ASan+UBSan(+LSan) MCP/nostr 9/9; relay suites x8 repeat clean. Protocol review: no blocking smells; residual (accepted AUTH then persistent auth-required stays held; stale CLOSED across reconnect) filed md-quhj.

title: validate-client.py: repeat cell exactly-once and post-drain negatives
description: Low J/F from the md-cdz Nostr protocol review (client-validation.md). Run.correlated() requires every earlier request_id to be ignored as history at least once, not exactly once (would also prove event.id dedup on replay). Its 'never answered history / never REJECTED' negatives are checked once after the session streams, not after finish_host/finish_client drain to EOF. Test hardening only; history precedes the host's EOSE boundary, so current checks are complete in practice.

title: ScreenCaptureKit backend: honour MdCaptureConfig.output (display selection)
description: Why: md-346 added MdCaptureConfig.output (documented as DXGI-only; host --capture-output errors on non-Windows). capture_screencapturekit.m always captures shareableContent.displays[0]. What: accept an index or display ID/name in SCK, fail init clearly on unknown selections, then allow --capture-output on macOS.

CGEvent input is mapped into the selected display's CG bounds, and agent actions are inverse-mapped. title: DXGI: capture all outputs as one virtual desktop
description: Why: md-346 made the DXGI output selectable (index/device name, default primary) but deliberately did not add an all-outputs mode: it needs one IDXGIOutputDuplication per output (possibly on different adapters/devices), compositing differently sized/rotated modes into one virtual-desktop staging buffer, per-output damage and pointer ownership (DXGI reports Visible only on the output holding the pointer), and matching input mapping. What: design first (single combined frame vs. per-output streams), then implement in capture_dxgi.cpp with a selector such as 'all'. Depends on the input virtual-desktop mapping bead.
close_reason: Committed on feat/windows-w65-dbg-246: --capture-output all composes every output (per-output devices/duplications, rotation) into one bounding-rect frame with black gaps; output_rect = bounding rect so input maps linearly; MS-sample pointer ownership; sweep wait with documented frame-interval poll limit. Synthetic layout/composition/pointer tests + console all-mode cells; real multi-monitor not covered (VM). Follow-up md-pvlj.

title: MCP: decide hold-vs-close for live SSE streams while host-allowlist readiness is down
description: Follow-up from md-ht7 protocol review. Since md-ht7, every allowlist readiness transition wakes the transport; while readiness is not LOADED (every relay disconnected/CLOSED, or history being re-delivered after reconnect) host_mcp_acl_grant() denies, so all live-admitted SSE streams are closed at once. This is consistent with the documented fail-closed rule (POSTs get 401 in the same window) and the proxy recovers via reconnect+backoff after EOSE, but with a single --relay every relay reconnect churns all live streams. Options: (a) keep (document recommending >=2 relays); (b) on non-LOADED, withhold delivery but keep streams open and re-check on the next LOADED version (needs a tri-state grant result from the source instead of 0). Touches src/host/mcp_nostr_acl.c, src/core/mcp_http.c sse_regrant_locked, docs/mcp-auth.md.
close_reason: Implemented option (b) as hold/quarantine (ca91715): live-list SSE streams are held (open, no frames) while the allowlist is unknown and re-evaluated on the next LOADED wake-up (close if agent lost / one list_changed if tool set changed / silent resume). New MD_MCP_GRANT_UNKNOWN contract + md_nostr_granted_capabilities_known() (grant+readiness under one lock; stopped bridge = deny). Only bound: SSE-capacity eviction of a held stream by a non-live newcomer (event-tied, no timer). Option (a) evidence: >=2 relays does not avoid the window, a reconnecting relay is 'pending' until its EOSE (update_acl_readiness). Tests: test_mcp_http, private-relay mcp-proxy e2e with real relay drop, test_nostr. macOS 38/38 (all signer backends), Linux 39 ok/1 env skip parallel+serial, ASan/LSan/UBSan clean on MCP+nostr tests. Protocol review: no polling/timers/new REQ; follow-up md-ip2k (terminal CLOSED holds indefinitely).

title: client: SDL opengl renderer segfaults on Wayland without libOpenGL.so.0; add GLES2 fallback

Windows VM DXGI pointer repaint timing (md-v9wt, 2026-11-19, traced per AcquireNextFrame): SetCursor reaches DXGI as a pointer-only update ~1 ms later (LastPresentTime 0, LastMouseUpdateTime set), before DWM repaints. After a software cursor (monochrome; masked color, which DWM reduces to monochrome: green->black, blue->white, mask quadrants exact), DWM erases it in a separate present 2-47 ms later with a dirty rect equal to the old cursor rect, so the first composited frame of a following color (hardware) pointer shows the old cursor under its transparent pixels. While the console display is off DWM presents nothing and DXGI reports the pointer Visible=0 at 0,0, then re-sends Visible=1 plus the shape right after the wake; the erase is folded into the wake's full [0,0-1024,768] redraw. drain_to_idle(300) ends ~100 ms before the console's next power-off (phase lock), so power-offs right after a change are common, not rare. Under host load a shape update can arrive in the same AcquireNextFrame as DWM's erase present (1 of 80). A frame's timestamp is LastPresentTime when the desktop changed, otherwise LastMouseUpdateTime: an exact pointer-only test. To debug, #include a tracing copy of capture_dxgi.cpp that logs FrameInfo plus GetFrameDirtyRects; the test TU already includes the .cpp.
